title: 1 Chronicles Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on 1 Chronicles 4: the families of Judah, the prayer of Jabez, and the towns and conquests of Simeon.

questions.text: What was the name of the sister of Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash?
questions.explanation: The sons of the father of Etam were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, and the name of their sister was Hazzelelponi.

questions.text: Who were the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa?
questions.explanation: Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.

questions.text: Why did Jabez's mother give him that name?
questions.explanation: His mother named him Jabez, saying, "Because I bore him with sorrow."

answers.text: "Because he came in the time of harvest"

questions.text: In his prayer, what did Jabez ask God to enlarge?
questions.explanation: Jabez asked God to bless him and enlarge his border, and God granted him what he requested.

questions.text: What does verse 14 say the people of Ge Harashim were?
questions.explanation: Seraiah became the father of Joab the father of Ge Harashim, for they were craftsmen.

questions.text: Bithiah, whom Mered took, was the daughter of whom?
questions.explanation: Verse 18 speaks of the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered took.

questions.text: Who lived at Netaim and Gederah with the king for his work?
questions.explanation: These were the potters and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah; they lived there with the king for his work.

questions.text: How many children did Shimei have?
questions.explanation: Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children.

questions.text: What did the Simeonites find when they went to the entrance of Gedor?
questions.explanation: They went to seek pasture for their flocks and found fat and good pasture, and the land was wide, quiet and peaceful.

questions.text: Whom did the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir strike?
questions.explanation: Five hundred men of Simeon went to Mount Seir and struck the remnant of the Amalekites who escaped, and lived there.
